issues.legal_issue: Rights granted by a proprietor in estate land or forest produce cease on statutory vesting and cannot be enforced against the State unless they fall within an interest saved by the governing Act.
material_facts: Proprietors granted rights to propagate lac, collect tendu leaves, and gather fruits and flowers from trees in their estates.
After statutory notifications, the State took possession of the estates and refused to recognise the grantees’ rights.
The claimed rights were derived from the proprietors and were not shown to fall within any of the interests saved by the Act.
issues.conclusion: The rights ceased upon vesting and could not be enforced against the State; the appeals were allowed and the earlier decision in Chhotabhai Jethabhai Patel and Co. was overruled.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 4(1)(a) of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950, proprietary rights and interests derived through a proprietor vest in the State free of encumbrances and cease, notwithstanding a contract, grant, or document. The interests saved are those specified in section 5(a)–(h); a claimant must bring the claimed interest within those provisions. The Court applied Shrimati Shantabai v. State of Bombay and Mahadeo v. State of Bombay, and overruled Chhotabhai Jethabhai Patel and Co. v. State of Madhya Pradesh.

rule.if: abolition_vesting_dispute and proprietor_derived_estate_right and state_took_possession_after_vesting and not interest_within_statutory_savings

predicates.abolition_vesting_dispute: The case concerns whether rights in an estate remain enforceable against the State after statutory abolition and vesting.
predicates.proprietor_derived_estate_right: A person acquired a right in estate land or its produce from a proprietor or through a proprietor.
predicates.state_took_possession_after_vesting: The State took possession of the estate after the statutory vesting event.
predicates.interest_within_statutory_savings: The claimed interest falls within an interest expressly preserved by the governing enactment.

issues.definition: When a vesting dispute concerns a right derived from a proprietor, the State has taken possession after vesting, and the right is not within the statutory savings, the right is not enforceable against the State.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision making certain transfers void from vesting does not make an earlier transfer binding on the State or prevent the transferred interest from vesting in the State.
material_facts: The grantees claimed rights transferred to them by proprietors before the estates vested in the State.
They argued that the provision addressing transfers of rights liable to vest preserved their earlier transfers against the State.
The Act separately provided for vesting and specified the interests that could be saved.
issues.conclusion: The provision did not save the earlier transfers from vesting or require the State to recognise them; it only addressed the voidness from vesting of the transfers it covered.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950, provides that transfers of rights liable to vest, made after the specified cutoff, are void from the date of vesting. It does not provide that a transfer made before that cutoff binds the State. Such a transfer may be recognised, and compensation may be available under the Act, but section 6 does not itself preserve the interest against vesting under sections 3 and 4(1)(a). The interests preserved are those specified in section 5(a)–(h).

predicates.abolition_vesting_dispute: The case concerns whether a transfer of an interest in an estate binds the State after statutory abolition and vesting.
predicates.proprietor_transfer_before_vesting: A proprietor transferred a right to another person before the estate vested in the State.
predicates.transfer_of_right_liable_to_vest: The transferred right was an interest liable to vest in the State under the governing enactment.

issues.definition: An earlier transfer of a right liable to vest does not, merely because it preceded vesting, make that right binding on the State.
